import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Create a synthetic dataset of monthly adjusted close prices from 2010 to 2023
date_range = pd.date_range(start='2010-01-01', end='2023-12-01', freq='MS')
np.random.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
prices = np.random.normal(loc=100, scale=10, size=len(date_range)).cumsum()  # Simulated prices

# Create a DataFrame
synthetic_data = pd.DataFrame({'Date': date_range, 'Adjusted_Close': prices})

# Display the first few rows of the synthetic dataset
synthetic_data.head()

from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller

# Perform the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test
adf_result = adfuller(synthetic_data['Adjusted_Close'])

# Extract the test statistic and p-value
adf_statistic = adf_result[0]
p_value = adf_result[1]

adf_statistic, p_value

# Apply differencing to the data
synthetic_data['Differenced'] = synthetic_data['Adjusted_Close'].diff().dropna()

# Perform the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test again on the differenced data
adf_result_diff = adfuller(synthetic_data['Differenced'].dropna())

# Extract the test statistic and p-value
adf_statistic_diff = adf_result_diff[0]
p_value_diff = adf_result_diff[1]

adf_statistic_diff, p_value_diff

from arch import arch_model

# Fit a GARCH(1, 1) model to the differenced data
model = arch_model(synthetic_data['Differenced'].dropna(), vol='Garch', p=1, q=1)
garch_fit = model.fit(disp="off")

# Forecast the next 12 months
forecast = garch_fit.forecast(horizon=12)
forecasted_values = forecast.mean.iloc[-1].values

forecasted_values

from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA

# Fit an ARIMA model to the differenced data
# We'll use order (p, d, q) = (1, 1, 1) as a starting point
arima_model = ARIMA(synthetic_data['Adjusted_Close'], order=(1, 1, 1))
arima_fit = arima_model.fit()

# Forecast the next 12 months
arima_forecast = arima_fit.forecast(steps=12)
arima_forecast

# Create a synthetic test set with known values for the next 12 months
# For simplicity, let's assume the known values are slightly higher than the forecasted values
known_values = arima_forecast + np.random.normal(loc=5, scale=2, size=12)

# Calculate RMSE
rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((arima_forecast - known_values) ** 2))

known_values, rmse
